CHAPTER 1
INTRODUCTION
SECTION I : DATA COLLECTION TECHNIQUE
 Purpose of the Publication
 User Guide to Indian Police Statistics
● Statistics Covered
 Data source and quality
● Data Collection Tool
● Analytical Techniques
● Data Collection Procedure
 Data Limitations and Implications
● Conventions used
This section provides information regarding the purpose of publication, user guide to
Indian Police Statistics, data source and quality, statistical tools, procedure of data collection,
limitations and implications.
PURPOSE OF PUBLICATION:
The BPR&D has been publishing the “Data on Police Organizations” in India, since 1986,
annually. From time to time, some of the important features like woman police, police
expenditure, constabulary ratio, transport facilities, communication facilities, representation of
SCs/STs and police training centers were added.
```
In this publication, dimensions like infrastructure of CAPFs (vehicle availability, family
```
```
quarters, training institutions, tracker and sniffer dogs and pay scales), Gender- wise data on
```
Police Forces, District Armed Reserve Police, Senior Supervisory Officers, Immediate Supervisory
Officers and Field Staff Ratio, Data of Woman Police, Sanctioned and Actual Strength of SCs/
STs and OBCs have been added.
22
This issue of, “Data on Police Organizations” in India, as on 01.01.2020, will be more useful
for the users, especially for the policy makers, police officers, researchers, academicians, police
administrators and other stakeholders, as it is coming out timely.
DATA COLLECTION PROCEDURE:-
```
“Data on Police Organizations” in India (DoPO), has been prepared on the basis of the
```
data provided by the States/UTs, CAPFs and other Central Police Organizations. Further, data
```
have also been obtained from the Registrar General of India (RGI) and the Survey of India (SOI).
```
STATISTICAL TOOLS:-
Statistical methods involved in carrying out the study include-planning, designing,
collection of data, analyzing, drawing meaningful interpretation and reporting of the findings.
PRESENTATION OF DATA:-
Data are collected in a raw format. However, in this format, there are inherent difficulties in
its understanding. Therefore, data have been summarized, processed, analyzed, and presented
in charts and tables to make it more meaningful.
Graph is a very effective visual tool, as it displays data at a glance, facilitates comparison,
reveals trends and relationships within the data, such as changes over time, frequency
distribution and correlation, etc. Bar graphs, Pie charts and other statistical tools have been
used.
DATA LIMITATIONS:-
DoPO has been prepared on the basis of data provided by the States/UTs/CAPFs and
other Police Organizations.
Police structure in different States/UTs, CAPFs and CPOs is not uniform. In a few cases,
States/UTs have not provided complete data, consequently, it has been mentioned as ‘Not
```
Available (NA)/Not Provided (NP)’in the relevant Tables and, at places, wherever relevant, data
```
of the previous year has been incorporated for the sake of comparison.
CHAPTER 1 - INTRODUCTION
23
SECTION II : INDIAN DEMOGRAPHY
 Male & Female Population
 Geographical Area
This section depicts the information/data of States/UTs in respect of demography,
containing male-female population and geographical area of the country.
MALE & FEMALE POPULATION
Demography is the statistical study of populations, especially human beings. At a glance,
it analyzes living population, i.e., changes over time and space in response to birth, migration,
aging, death, etc.
Its analysis covers complete society or groups defined by criteria such as education,
nationality, religion and ethnicity, etc. Demographic studies also analyze the relationships
between economic, social, cultural and biological processes influencing the population.
The total population of India, as on 01.10.2019, as provided by the Registrar General of
India and the Census Commissioner of India is 134.3 crore, approx., comprising 69.1 crore males
and 65.2 crore females.
Among the States, Uttar Pradesh, with a population of more than 22.67 crore, holds the
distinction of being the most populous state in the country, followed by Maharashtra, with a
population of 12.28 crore.
Among the Union Territories, Delhi, with a population of more than 2.00 crore, holds the
distinction of being the most populous UT in the country, followed by J&K, with a population
of 1.33 crore.
GEOGRAPHICAL AREA
The total geographical area of the country is 32,87,162 Sq. Kms, approximately. The largest
state in India, in terms of geographical area, is Rajasthan, with an area of 3,42,111 Sq. Km. and
the smallest is the UT of Lakshadweep, with an area of 30 Sq. Km.

Battalions in the country.

Table 2.1.1. It also gives the percentage of changes with reference to the preceding years from
2014 to 2019.

The CRPF assists the State governments in maintenance of Law and Order and performs
various internal security duties. BSF, ITBP, Assam rifles and SSB are border guarding forces, but
they also provide need based assistance to the civil administration for maintenance of law and
order and internal security.

management plan of the Police forces, generally, comparing Senior Supervisory Officers

Availability of adequate number of women in police is essential for reducing the
vulnerability of women against crimes. The existing Woman Police Population Ratio is still very
low. Poor representation of women in police is posing serious challenges in dealing with crimes
against women and woman criminals. Therefore, it is essential that woman Police personnel
are visible at the cutting edge level.

The total strength of Women in police from 2014 to 2019 has shown an increasing trend,
which is self-explanatory from the following graph.

CHAPTER 4
POLICE BUDGET
SECTION I : BUDGET & EXPENDITURE ON STATE/UT POLICE
 Police Expenditure
 Training Expenditure
 Modernization Grants
This section provides information regarding the total Budget of States/UTs, expenditure by
the States/UTs on Police forces, expenditure on Police training as well as modernization grants
by the Central Government and the State Governments. The UTs of A&N Islands, Chandigarh,
D&N Haveli, Daman & Diu, Delhi, Lakshadweep and Puducherry are directly financed by the
Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
EXPENDITURE OF STATE/UT POLICE FORCES
The sanctioned strength of State Police Forces has increased to 26.23 lakh in 2019 over
25.95 lakh in 2018 and the expenditure on State Police Forces has increased to Rs. 1,38,794.32
```
crore in the year 2019-20, from Rs. 1,34,261.90 crore (revised) in the year 2018-19. Details are
```
given at Table No. 4.1.3.
EXPENDITURE ON POLICE TRAINING
An amount of Rs.1,566.85 crore was spent on police training at the all India level in the
year 2019-20, out of the total police expenditure of Rs. 1,38,794.32 crore during the same year.
The maximum expenditure on training, i.e Rs. 203.92 crore, was made by the Delhi Police.
Details are given at Table No. 4.1.3.
TRENDS IN POLICE TRAINING EXPENDITURE
Expenditure on Police Training from 2011-12 to 2019-20 has shown mixed trends. It
increased from 2011-12 to 2014-15 but then declined in 2014-15 & 2015-16 and has again
42
increased from 2016-2017 to 2018-19, as shown in the graph given below:-

MODERNIZATION GRANTS TO THE STATE POLICE FORCES
Modernization grants to the state police forces, allocated by the MHA, are meant to
upgrade the infrastructure of the state police in order to improve their capacity to meet the
emerging challenges of internal security, besides improving efficiency and effectiveness in
Police service delivery.
The focus of the scheme is on strengthening of the police infrastructure by way of
construction of secure and people friendly Police Stations, Police Outposts, Police Housing,
Improved Mobility, Modern Weaponry, Computerization, Communication Equipment, Modern
Traffic Control Equipment, etc.
At the national level, the grants made available to the state police forces in the financial
year 2019-20 by the Central Government and the State Governments and the total amount
utilized for modernization by the State Governments for the State Police Forces are given at
Table No. 4.1.4.

TRANSPORT FACILITIES (MOBILITY)
```
Mobility is measured in terms of the ability of vehicles to move the complete strength of
a Police unit on the call of duty. Police mobility is directly linked with its operational efficiency.
Quick response of police forces, during law and order situations, helps significantly in protecting
life and property of the people.
Vehicles required to provide mobility to Police Forces have been divided into four
```
categories, i.e., Heavy Vehicles (buses/trucks, troop carriers, etc.), Medium Vehicles, Light
```
```
Vehicles (jeeps/cars, etc.) and Very Light Vehicles (three/two Wheelers). Heavy, Medium and
```
Light vehicles cater to the requirements of the Police Stations and field level supervisory and
senior supervisory officers.
Apart from these vehicles, state police have also procured some Special Purpose Vehicles
```
like Mines Protected Vehicles (MPV), riot control vehicles, ambulances, mobile forensic vans,
```
water cannons, water tankers, Prison vans, etc., to meet their specific needs. These vehicles
have been clubbed under the ‘Other Category.’
In all, 2,02,925 vehicles were available with State/UT Police Force in 2019, This number
has decreased from 2,04,807 during the year 2018. Out of the total of 2,02,925 vehicles, 11,956
are Heavy duty Vehicles, 19,536 Medium duty Vehicles, 81,099 Light Vehicles, 87,586 Very Light
```
Vehicles (two/ three wheelers) and 2,748 are Other Vehicles. Details are given at Table No. 5.1.6
```

Police manpower alone is not sufficient to curb crime, maintain law and order, traffic
management, internal security and other policing requirements. Therefore, they are required
to be supplemented with modern facilities and gadgets like computers, CCTV cameras, traffic
and investigation equipment, speedometers, breath analyzers and forensic science kits/labs,
etc. to enhance their effectiveness and efficiency.

The number of Sub-Inspectors (SIs) recruited during 2019 were 12,909, whereas this figure

followed by 2,645 in Jharkhand. Details are given at Table No. 6.1.8.
TRAINING OF NEWLY RECRUITED POLICE PERSONNEL
A total number of 1,35,151 newly recruited Police Personnel from the rank of Constables
```
to the Dy.SP (Civil, District Armed Reserve and Special Armed police) were trained during 2019
```
in State Police Training Institutes. The break-up is 1,10,719 Constables, 4408 Head Constables,
117 ASI, 16,011 SIs, 358 Dy.SP and 3538 Any others. Details are given at Table No. 6.1.10.
The highest number i.e., 6151 SIs were trained by the U.P Police, followed by 2504 SIs by
Jharkhand. As far as Constables are concerned, 40,726 Constables were trained in UP, followed
by 10,690 from Rajasthan.

20 Punjab 3 Dial- 112 (ERSS) In Indian historically, we have had different phone
```
numbers to call Police, Fire & Ambulance services
namely 100, 102, 103, which are not routed to a Centrally
Emergency Response Dispatcher. This leads to confusion
in the public about emergency contact number. To
provide for speedy Justice and enhanced punishment
for Criminals in sexual assault cases of extreme nature,
Ministry of Home Affairs, Govt. of India has started one
single Helpline Dial-112 under Emergency Response
```
Support System (ERSS) to call Police, Fire and Ambulance
```
Services. The project is conceived to bridge the existing
gaps and meet the current challenges being faced by
major police force in the country for an immediate
emergency response system specifically inclined
towards WOMAN issues.
181-Women Helpline What’app
```
(769618181)
```
Dial-181 Punjab Police Helpline is helpline as well as
State-wide grievance redressal platform, which provides
round-the-clock assistance to women, children, senior
citizens, NRIs and other citizens who are in need of police
rsponses, support and assistance.It provides a free and
easy way for the citizens to share various police-related
concers and grievences, follow up on their complaints
made to different police units and offices, and provide
valuable feedback on the functioning of the Police to
District Police Chiefs, Senior Police Officers as well as the
higher authorities.
